Z3 inputs: https://zenodo.org/records/16740866/files/QF_LIA.tar.zst?download=1
Z3 commit message: smt: do not distribute a conjunction that already has a literal in flatten_clauses

The occurrence count introduced in #11291 only sees the clauses that are
pending in the current round. A conjunction (not (or b1 .. bn)) that is
shared with an assertion of an earlier check-sat call, and so already has a
literal in the context, looks unique in every later round and is distributed
again on each incremental call: O(N*K) clauses for N conjuncts and K
assertions instead of O(N+K).

Require in addition that the disjunction (or b1 .. bn) has reference count 1,
i.e. the negation is its only parent. This is the sharing test that
flatten_clauses used before #11291, without the exemption for literal
co-disjuncts. The disjunction gets another parent when it occurs positively,
as in (or d x) after splitting (ite d x y), and when smt::context internalizes
it. The reference count of the negation itself is not usable: the rewriter
caches of asserted_formulas and the assertion kept alive by the front end
raise it for ordinary unshared clauses.

Add a unit test covering an unshared clause with a live root, the n*m shape of
#11291, and incremental reuse with a theory atom and with a Boolean constant.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
